summary: No training activity data has been recorded over the last 4 weeks, making it impossible to assess current fitness or accumulated fatigue from Garmin metrics. The limited body battery data available (Nov 17–21) shows very low values — peaking at just 7–49 — which suggests significant fatigue or low recovery, particularly concerning given today's planned 4-hour long ride. With the Marathon 78 days away (target sub-4h at 5:45/km), the immediate priority must be establishing consistent aerobic run volume while managing overall load carefully.
suggestions: Given the critically low body battery readings (max 7–49) in the days leading into today's planned 240-min long ride, seriously consider reducing today's session to 60–90 minutes at easy Z2 power (128–155W) to avoid digging a deeper fatigue hole before the training week begins.

With the Marathon 78 days away and no recorded training visible, treat the next 4 weeks as a disciplined aerobic base rebuild — prioritise completing the planned long runs (20–22km) consistently at 6:15–6:45/km before adding any negative-split or tempo overlays.

Ensure the Thursday tempo runs (5:35–5:50/km, 30–40 min) are genuinely achievable at that pace before race day; if they feel forced, back off to 5:50–6:00/km — arriving at the Marathon undertrained but fresh beats arriving injured.

Start logging sleep and wellness data consistently — with no activity or wellness baseline for most of the past 4 weeks, it is impossible to make data-driven adjustments to load; even manual daily notes will help identify recovery patterns.

The swimming sessions (2km+ at ≤2:30/100m) are well below the Ironman Cervia swim requirement (3800m at 1:50/100m), but that race is 211 days away — keep swim sessions as planned for now and revisit volume and pace targets in January.
